sections.title: Contracting Approaches for Anchored Systems
sections.summary: Three contracting approaches: (1) Method — owner specifies all details; contractor constructs per drawings; maximum owner control; (2) Performance — owner provides geometry and performance criteria; specialty contractor designs; most common in U.S.; may be pre-bid or post-bid; (3) Design-build — specialty contractor designs and constructs per owner requirements; minimum owner design control. Each agency should develop a formal anchored system contracting policy.
sections.body:
Each owner should develop a formal policy on anchored system design and contracting. Policy objectives include: uniformity in selection of anchored systems; standard policies for design review; and appropriate allocation of design responsibility.

Method approach: Owner prepares complete design and construction drawings. Contract documents include drawings with soldier beam type/size/spacing, lagging thickness, anchor type/inclination/unbonded length/bond length for each anchor. Specifications define materials, testing requirements, and acceptance criteria. Less common for anchored walls because it requires the owner to have access to specialty expertise and local knowledge of anchor capacity.

Performance approach: Owner establishes scope of work and prepares drawings showing project geometry, subsurface conditions, and performance requirements (design life, tolerable movements, anchor testing requirements and acceptance criteria, corrosion protection requirements). The specialty contractor designs the system to meet these requirements. Two sub-approaches: (1) pre-bid typical section design — owner prepares typical section with specific dimensions that can be used as-bid; (2) post-bid design — contractor submits design after award. The owner should include a generic design in the bid documents for general contractors to decide whether to use it or propose a specialty contractor design.

Contractor design/build: Owner outlines project requirements, obtains subsurface information, and provides quality assurance. Specialty contractor designs and constructs the entire system. Owner retains QA responsibility but relinquishes design control.
key_points: Three approaches: method (owner-designed), performance (contractor-designed to owner specs), design-build
Performance approach most common in U.S. — provides specialty contractor flexibility and expertise
Performance contract must specify: geometry, design life, corrosion protection, tolerable movements, testing and acceptance criteria
Agency should include a generic design in bid documents for general contractors to price the work
sections.applicability: Contract document preparation and responsibility allocation for anchored wall projects
